title: Gaurav Sharma v. State of U.P. & 4 Others
coram: Shashi Kant Gupta & Ajit Kumar, JJ.
disposition: Writ petition allowed (refusal quashed; connection to be reconsidered)
headnote: Under Section 43(1) of the Electricity Act, 2003, an owner or occupier of any premises has a statutory right to a connection, and the licensee a corresponding duty to supply. Clause 4.4 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 and the Indemnity Bond (Annexure 4.2) enable a genuine occupier — including a family member in separate possession who cannot obtain the owner's NOC — to obtain a connection; the object of the bond is only to exclude a trespasser or house-grabber. A connection cannot be refused merely because of a family dispute or the absence of the owner's consent.

holding_units.code: U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 (with s.43(1), Electricity Act 2003)
holding_units.topic: Connection to a genuine occupier on an indemnity bond, without the owner's NOC
holding_units.question: Can a licensee refuse a connection to a genuine occupier (a son in separate possession) because the owner (his father) refuses consent amid a family dispute?
holding_units.holding: No. Section 43(1) confers on an occupier a statutory right to supply; Clause 4.4 read with Annexure 4.2 lets a genuine occupier unable to obtain the owner's NOC furnish an indemnity bond and obtain a connection. The object of the bond is only to exclude a trespasser/house-grabber; a family dispute or want of the owner's consent is no ground to refuse. Refusal quashed and remitted for reconsideration.
holding_units.limiting_facts: The petitioner, a son in separate possession of one of his father's houses (paying house tax), was refused a connection because the father declined to give an NOC amid a family dispute.

principle_tags.application: A genuine occupier (including a family member in separate possession) has a statutory right under s.43(1) to a connection and may furnish an indemnity bond (Annexure 4.2) where the owner's NOC is unavailable; the bond only excludes trespassers/house-grabbers.

lead_authorities.name: Seema Mansoor v. U.P. Power Corporation

authorities.name: Seema Mansoor v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. & Others
authorities.proposition: Under Clause 4.4 and Annexure 4.2 of the Code, a lessee/tenant/occupier cannot be refused a connection merely for want of the landlord's consent; the indemnity bond enables the occupier to obtain supply.
authorities.how_treated: Followed as the governing authority on the occupier's entitlement.

authorities.name: Smt. Sushama Chowdhary v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. & 4 Others
authorities.citation: Misc. Bench No. 9588 of 2014 (Allahabad HC, DB)
authorities.proposition: Section 43(1) casts an affirmative obligation on the licensee to supply an owner or occupier; Clause 4.4 is in aid of that duty, and an occupier who cannot get the owner's consent may furnish an indemnity bond (Annexure 4.2).
authorities.how_treated: Relied on and quoted for the s.43(1) obligation and the indemnity-bond route.

authorities.name: Chandu Khamaru v. Smt. Nayan Malik
authorities.proposition: Under Section 43(1), a distribution licensee has a statutory duty to supply an owner or occupier who applies, and the occupier a corresponding statutory right; a family dispute does not deprive a person of a connection.
authorities.how_treated: Relied on (through Sushama Chowdhary) for the statutory right of an occupier.
